message.content:
**Hydrogen – Key Properties**

| Property | Value / Description |
|----------|---------------------|
| **Atomic number** | 1 |
| **Symbol** | H |
| **Common isotope** | Protium (^1H) – 99.98 % natural abundance |
| **Other stable isotopes** | Deuterium (^2H, D) – ~0.015 %; Tritium (^3H, T) – radioactive, half‑life ≈12.32 yr |
| **Atomic mass** | 1.00794 u (average weighted by natural isotopic composition) |
| **Electron configuration** | 1s¹ |
| **Electronegativity (Pauling)** | 2.20 |
| **First ionization energy** | 13.598 eV (1312 kJ/mol) |
| **Second ionization energy** | 27.211 eV (2625 kJ/mol) |
| **Electron affinity** | –72.8 kJ/mol (negative, meaning energy is released when H⁻ forms) |
| **Boiling point** | –252.87 °C (20.28 K) at 1 atm |
| **Melting point** | –259.16 °C (14.01 K) at 1 atm |
| **Density at STP** | 0.08988 g/L (≈0.0000899 kg/m³) |
| **Molar volume at STP** | 22.414 L/mol |
| **State at room temperature** | Gas (colorless, odorless, tasteless) |
| **Bond type** | Forms covalent bonds; diatomic molecules (H₂) are nonpolar but highly reactive due to small size and high mobility |
| **Reactivity** | Extremely flammable; reacts vigorously with oxygen (forming water), halogens, and many metals; forms hydrides with electropositive elements |
| **Uses** | Fuel cell technology, ammonia synthesis (Haber process), petroleum refining, metal reduction, laboratory reagent, cryogenic applications (liquid hydrogen as propellant) |

**Interesting Notes**

* Hydrogen’s low mass gives it the highest average speed among gases at a given temperature (Maxwell–Boltzmann distribution).
* Its small size allows it to diffuse through many materials, making it useful for leak detection (using tracer gas techniques).
* In its liquid form, hydrogen has a very low density (~70 kg/m³) and extremely low viscosity, which makes it attractive for high‑efficiency propulsion systems.

Feel free to let me know if you’d like deeper details on any specific property or application!
